concepts.label: vBucket hash table
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the per-vBucket in-memory hash table that 'hash' and 'hash detail' report aggregate/per-vBucket depth and size statistics for. This is the mechanism the whole command exists to expose, not any one of avg_count/max_depth/size/etc individually - those stay as prose/evidence detail rather than becoming their own concepts, per this round's tightened rule.

relations.subject: server:vbucket
relations.evidence: Provides information about the vBucket hash tables.

relations.subject: server:vbucket-hash-table
relations.evidence: It is also possible to get more detailed hash tables stats by using 'hash detail'. This prints per-vbucket stats.

notable_absence.finding: The page states the cost directly - 'Requesting these stats does affect performance, so don't do it too regularly' - but gives no quantification or guidance on what 'too regularly' means: no suggested polling interval, no numeric threshold, unlike the explicit numeric thresholds cbstats-config reports for other subsystems (e.g. bloom-filter residency thresholds).

cross_component_finding: The page draws a direct causal line from a structural stat to end-user-visible performance - 'if your hash table is tuned to have too few buckets for the data load within it, the max_depth will be too large, and performance will suffer' - the closest thing in this batch to an explanation of WHY a stat group matters rather than just what each field means, and the only page in this batch that states a stat's practical failure mode in prose rather than leaving it to the reader to infer from a bare description column.
cross_product_finding: Not applicable - no cross-product content on this page.
